questions.q: Why did Samuel pour a flask of oil on Saul’s head and kiss him?
questions.a: He did this because Yahweh had anointed Saul to be a ruler over his inheritance.

questions.q: What future event did Samuel share with Saul?
questions.a: Samuel told Saul that he would find two men near Rachel’s tomb who would tell him that the donkeys had been found.

questions.q: What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to the oak of Tabor?
questions.a: Three men going up to God at Bethel would meet him and give him two loaves of bread, which he should take.

questions.q: What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to Gibeah of God?
questions.a: The Spirit of Yahweh would rush upon him, he would prophesy with a group of prophets, and he would be changed into a different man.

questions.q: What instructions did Samuel give to Saul for later?
questions.a: Samuel told Saul to go down to Gilgal and wait seven days for Samuel to come and offer sacrifices.

questions.q: What happened when Saul turned his back to leave Samuel?
questions.a: When Saul turned to leave, God changed Saul’s inner being.

questions.q: Why did people wonder if Saul was one of the prophets?
questions.a: They saw him prophesying with the prophets and wondered how this had happened to the son of Kish.

questions.q: What did Saul tell his uncle when he was asked where he had gone?
questions.a: Saul told his uncle that when he and his servant could not find the donkeys, they went to Samuel.

questions.q: What did Saul not tell his uncle about what Samuel had said to him?
questions.a: Saul did not tell his uncle about the matter of the kingship.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh say that Israel had rejected him?
questions.a: Israel had rejected Yahweh because they had asked for a king to be set over them.

questions.q: What happened when Saul, the son of Kish, was chosen as the next king?
questions.a: They looked for Saul, but he could not be found.

questions.q: Where was Saul when he was chosen as the next king?
questions.a: Saul had hidden himself among the bags.

questions.q: What did Samuel say about the man whom Yahweh had chosen?
questions.a: Samuel said that there was no one like Saul among all the people.

questions.q: How were the customs of the kingship established and preserved?
questions.a: Samuel told the people the customs of the kingship, wrote them in a book, and placed the book before Yahweh.

questions.q: How did some wicked men show their dislike for Saul?
questions.a: Some wicked men despised Saul and did not bring him a gift.

commentary.text: Verses 1–8 The sacred anointing, then used, pointed at the great Messiah, or Anointed One, the King of the church, and High Priest of our profession, who was anointed with the oil of the Spirit, not by measure, but without measure, and above all the priests and princes of the Jewish church. For Saul's further satisfaction, Samuel gives him some signs which should come to pass the same day. The first place he directs him to, was the sepulchre of one of his ancestors; there he must be reminded of his own mortality, and now that he had a crown before him, must think of his grave, in which all his honour would be laid in the dust. From the time of Samuel there appears to have been schools, or places where pious young men were brought up in the knowledge of Divine things. Saul should find himself strongly moved to join with them, and should be turned into another man from what he had been. The Spirit of God changes men, wonderfully transforms them. Saul, by praising God in the communion of saints, became another man, but it may be questioned if he became a new man.

The signs Samuel had given Saul, came to pass punctually; he found that God had given him another heart, another disposition of mind. Yet let not an outward show of devotion, and a sudden change for the present, be too much relied on; Saul among the prophets was Saul still. His being anointed was kept private. He leaves it to God to carry on his own work by Samuel, and sits still, to see how the matter will fall.

Samuel tells the people, Ye have this day rejected your God. So little fond was Saul now of that power, which soon after, when he possessed it, he could not think of parting with, that he hid himself. It is good to be conscious of our unworthiness and insufficiency for the services to which we are called; but men should not go into the contrary extreme, by refusing the employments to which the Lord and the church call them. The greater part of the people treated the matter with indifference. Saul modestly went home to his own house, but was attended by a band of men whose hearts God disposed to support his authority. If the heart bend at any time the right way, it is because He has touched it. One touch is enough when it is Divine. Others despised him. Thus differently are men affected to our exalted Redeemer. There is a remnant who submit to him, and follow him wherever he goes; they are those whose hearts God has touched, whom he has made willing. But there are others who despise him, who ask, How shall this man save us? They are offended in him, and they will be punished.
